speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To begin my assessment, how long have you had these symptoms, and can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions in detail?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI). The combination of migratory polyarthralgia (knee), a new monoarthritis (wrist), fever, chills, and recent sexual activity is highly suggestive of gonococcal septic arthritis. I am requesting blood cultures and a Gram stain of the synovial fluid from the affected wrist.
